businessModel: Search-engine revenue share (mainly Google), plus Mozilla VPN/Monitor subscriptions and partnerships
paidNote: Free browser; optional paid Mozilla VPN and other subscriptions
updateCadence: Every 2 weeks since Firefox 155 (Sept 1, 2026; experiment), previously every 4 weeks; ESR ~yearly major
summary: The only major browser on its own engine: strong default tracker blocking, Total Cookie Protection, full MV2/uBlock Origin, vertical tabs, split view, profiles and an AI controls panel to block generative AI.
bestFor: Anyone who wants full uBlock Origin
Privacy-minded users who want sane defaults
People who want an independent engine, not Chromium
Power users who like about:config and add-ons
Android users who want desktop-style add-ons
notFor: People who rely on Chrome-only sites and web apps
Users who need the best battery life on laptops
Those who want a native passkey store or deep Google integration

pros.title: Full MV2 and uBlock Origin
pros.detail: Firefox supports both MV2 and MV3 extensions and is the recommended home of full uBlock Origin.

pros.title: Strong privacy defaults
pros.detail: Enhanced Tracking Protection, Total Cookie Protection, tracking-parameter stripping and optional Strict mode.

pros.title: AI controls
pros.detail: Since Firefox 148 a single AI controls section can block all current and future generative AI features.

pros.title: Modern tab tools
pros.detail: Vertical tabs (136), tab groups (137) and Split View (149) are built in.

pros.title: Independent engine
pros.detail: Gecko keeps the web from becoming a Chromium monoculture.

pros.title: Android add-ons
pros.detail: Firefox for Android installs desktop-grade add-ons from AMO.

cons.title: Smaller compatibility margin
cons.detail: Some sites are built and tested for Chrome first.

cons.title: Battery and memory
cons.detail: Efficient but behind Safari on laptops; no explicit Energy Saver control like Chrome.

cons.title: AI creep
cons.detail: Smart Window, sidebar chatbots and a free VPN add services, though all are optional.

cons.title: iOS is WebKit
cons.detail: Firefox for iOS must use Apple WebKit and has no extensions or Gecko benefits.

signatureFeatures: Enhanced Tracking Protection + Total Cookie Protection
Vertical tabs, tab groups and Split View
Free built-in browser VPN (50 GB/mo, rolling out)

faq.a: No. Firefox 159.0 shipped on Oct 27, 2026 (158.0.1 was Oct 20). With the new 2-week cadence Firefox 160 is due Nov 10, 2026.

faq.q: Can I turn off all AI in Firefox?
faq.a: Yes. Since Firefox 148 (Feb 24, 2026) the AI controls section in desktop settings can block all current and future generative AI features, or you can toggle individual ones such as the sidebar chatbot, link previews and Smart Window.

faq.q: Does Firefox still support uBlock Origin?
faq.a: Yes. Firefox supports MV2 and MV3 and Mozilla has said it will keep MV2 support; the uBlock Origin project recommends Firefox.

timeline.event: Phoenix 0.1; renamed Firefox in 2004 (1.0 in Nov 2004)
Firefox 136 ships vertical tabs; tab groups follow in 137 (April 2025)
Firefox 148 adds AI controls with an option to block all generative AI
Firefox 149 adds Split View, tab notes, a new Trust Panel and a free built-in VPN (50 GB/mo)
Release cadence moves to every two weeks (Firefox 155 on Sept 1); Smart Window beta rolls out in US/Canada/France
Firefox 159 (Oct 27) extends Smart Window with page monitoring and form drafting; Firefox Enterprise edition debuts with 158

switching.note: Imports from Chrome, Edge, Safari and others; Firefox Account sync handles the rest.

spec.codecs: H.264, VP9, AV1, HEVC (hardware where available), JPEG XL image support since 158
spec.sandbox: Multi-process with Fission site isolation and Rust components
spec.patchSpeed: Security fixes with each 2-week release plus out-of-band point releases (e.g. 158.0.1 on Oct 20)

graphics: WebGL strong, WebGPU shipping later than Chrome
memory: Lighter than Chrome in typical use
lowEnd: Runs on Windows 10 and old Macs via ESR
privacyDefaults: ETP Standard and TCP by default
blocking: Tracker blocking; uBO gives full blocking
media: DRM and PiP strong; no 4K Netflix
translation: Local translation, fewer languages than Google
extras: Free VPN and Smart Window beta
extensions: Full MV2 and MV3, mobile add-ons
passwords: Capable manager, no native passkey store
businessTrust: Nonprofit parent, but Google search revenue
ai: Smart Window, local features, all optional
